Nominating that same URL under this node's own id would be an over-claim, not a gain: candidate_urls would return distance 0, verify_base_graph.py would pass is_own_page=True, and the record would be relabelled 'name_labelled_on_own_official_page' — naturalresources.house.gov is the committee's page, not the subcommittee's. note: 'VA Medical Centers' is a curated template row, not a unit the VA names, and six readable VA pages say so. Probed 2026-09-18 with scripts/probe_candidate_pages.py: https://department.va.gov/integrated-service-networks/ (1,722 readable chars — the page the verifier already inherits for this node, and the one evidence.json records as its failure), https://department.va.gov/about/ (7,430), https://www.va.gov/health/ (9,441), https://www.va.gov/health-care/ (4,065) and https://www.va.gov/directory/guide/home.asp (1,766); https://www.va.gov/find-locations/ returned only 101 readable characters, below the verifier's 400-character floor, so it is not readable at all. None of them labels 'VA Medical Centers'. The networks page's own content wording for the layer it does describe is "Veterans Integrated Service Networks", and it carries no medical-centre layer beneath that. The node's own description gives the problem away — "Each VISN contains multiple VAMCs. Structure per VAMC: Director, Chief of Staff, ..." — it stands for the set of VISN 22's medical centres, which the VA names individually (VA San Diego, VA Long Beach, ...) and never collectively. Worth saying explicitly for whoever picks this up: a national VA page using the phrase 'VA medical centers' in prose would be the WRONG scope, not a fix — confirming a VISN-22 sub-grouping from a government-wide page is the same failure as matching 'Office of Science' inside 'Office of Science and Technology Policy'. Curation, not a URL.
